title: Complete Absence of Authentication & Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) on Session Endpoints
cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function, CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
owasp: API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization, API2:2023 Broken Authentication
evidence: GET /api/v1/research and /api/v1/research/{session_id} permit any unauthenticated caller to list, read, export, and delete any session from backend/data/sessions/.
impact: Complete loss of confidentiality and integrity for research sessions and uploaded documents across all users.
remediation: Introduce an authentication dependency (e.g. JWT or API key), bind sessions to tenant/user IDs, and verify that the requesting user owns the session before returning or deleting it.

title: Unauthenticated WebSocket Endpoint & Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH)
cwe: CWE-1385: Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets, CWE-306: Missing Authentication
evidence: websocket.py:25 unconditionally executes await ws.accept() without inspecting ws.headers.get('origin') or requiring an auth token in query/headers.
impact: A malicious website visited by a user can open a cross-site WebSocket to the local backend, initiate heavy research workflows, and read streaming LLM responses.
remediation: Validate the incoming Origin header against an explicit allowed-origin whitelist and require a short-lived authentication token upon connection handshake.

title: Unchecked Outbound HTTP Fetch with Redirects in Semantic Scholar PDF Fetcher (SSRF)
evidence: semantic_scholar_service.py:112-115 fetches arbitrary openAccessPdf URLs using httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True) without is_safe_url() validation.
impact: If an untrusted paper or external record supplies a malicious URL, the backend can be induced to query internal services (127.0.0.1:11434, 127.0.0.1:8000) or cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254).
remediation: Enforce WebScraperService.is_safe_url() or a shared IP validation filter before issuing requests in SemanticScholarService, and disable follow_redirects or validate destination IP at each redirect hop.

title: Synchronous Event-Loop Blocking & Unbounded PDF Page Extraction (Denial of Service)
cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption, CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits
evidence: pdf_service.py:147 iterates over reader.pages without a maximum page bound, and research.py:86 calls this synchronously inside an async route handler without asyncio.to_thread.
impact: Processing a multi-thousand-page or complex PDF freezes the main FastAPI asyncio event loop, causing denial of service for all active users and WebSocket streams.
remediation: Wrap all PDF extraction calls in asyncio.to_thread() and enforce a strict maximum page parsing limit (e.g. max 100 pages).

title: Prompt Delimiter Collision & Tag Escaping Vulnerability
cwe: CWE-116: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
evidence: Prompt templates wrap external strings in <untrusted_research_data> ... </untrusted_research_data> without stripping or escaping literal '</untrusted_research_data>' in paper titles, queries, or extracted text.
impact: Adversarial papers or user queries can prematurely terminate the untrusted data block and inject system-level directives to manipulate downstream analyst, critic, and builder agents.
remediation: Sanitize and escape closing delimiter tags from all untrusted inputs prior to embedding them in prompt templates.

title: Remote Code Execution Risk via Dynamic CDN Script Import in MermaidViewer
cwe: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere, CWE-79: Cross-Site Scripting
owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
evidence: MermaidViewer.tsx:26-27 executes new Function('url', 'return import(url)')('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs') to load and run unpinned JavaScript dynamically from a public CDN.
impact: If the third-party CDN is compromised, poisoned, or intercepted, malicious JavaScript runs with full privileges in the user's browser session. Bypasses CSP script-src nonces.
remediation: Install mermaid as an audited package dependency in package.json and bundle it locally with Next.js rather than importing arbitrary code at runtime.

title: Potential Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) DNS Rebinding in Web Scraper
evidence: is_safe_url() checks socket.getaddrinfo() before httpx.AsyncClient().get() initiates a secondary independent DNS resolution.
impact: A domain with a TTL of 0 seconds could resolve to a benign IP during validation and a private IP during HTTP fetch, though exploitation complexity via DuckDuckGo results is high.
remediation: Pin the resolved IP address in the HTTP client or configure a custom transport resolver that connects strictly to the validated IP.

title: Permissive Wildcard CORS Configuration with Credentials Enabled
cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-Domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
evidence: backend/core/config.py:14 defaults allowed_origins to ['*'] and backend/api/main.py:22 enables allow_credentials=True, causing Starlette to reflect the requesting origin.
impact: Any third-party website visited by a user can send credentialed requests to the backend API and read responses.
remediation: Restrict allowed_origins to explicit origins (e.g. ['http://localhost:3000']) when credentials are enabled.

title: Missing Standard HTTP Security Headers
evidence: FastAPI application lacks middleware injecting Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY.
impact: Increased susceptibility to clickjacking, MIME-confusion, and unconstrained script execution.
remediation: Add security header middleware or reverse-proxy header injection enforcing standard defensive headers.

title: Unbounded API Rate Limits and Resource Exhaustion
cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
evidence: No rate limiting middleware or request throttling is attached to /api/v1/research or /ws/research.
impact: An attacker or automated client can rapidly drain Groq LLM API quota (tokens per minute) or exhaust backend CPU/memory with parallel execution.
remediation: Implement slowapi or token bucket rate limiting on research initiation routes.

title: Backend Container Process Runs as Root
evidence: Dockerfile.backend does not define a non-root USER directive, causing the uvicorn process to run as root (uid 0) in the container.
impact: If an attacker achieves remote code execution or a container breakout, they execute with root privileges on the container system.
remediation: Add a non-root system user and group (e.g. appuser) and specify USER appuser before CMD in Dockerfile.backend.
